curation.notes: Multiplexed magnetic tweezers rotation-extension measurements on torsionally constrained 20.6 kbp (and 7.9 kbp control) dsDNA to measure salt-dependent DNA twist in up to 12 M LiCl, NaCl, KCl and CsCl, complemented by CD spectroscopy and all-atom MD simulations. Rotation curves at F = 0.25 pN from at least 11 molecules (LiCl) and typically 10–20 molecules per condition.

evidence.snippet: A frame grabber (PCIe 1433; National Instruments) collects images recorded at 58 Hz.
At each step of five applied turns, the extension of the tether is recorded for 6–10 s (at a camera rate of 58 Hz), and the mean extension is calculated.
we employ a pair of permanent magnets (5 × 5 × 5 mm3, Supermagnete, Switzerland) arranged in vertical geometry [47] with a gap of 1 mm
to bind 1.0 μm diameter streptavidin-coated magnetic beads (Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1, Thermo Fisher Scientific Baltics UAB, LT) and the flow cell surface, respectively.
We recorded extension–rotation curves by changing the magnet rotation, and thus the linking number ∆Lk, in steps of five turns at low force (F = 0.25 pN, unless stated otherwise).

handle_sequences.annotations: PCR-generated DNA fragments (~600 bp) labeled with multiple biotin or digoxigenin groups were ligated to the DNA (20.6 kbp or 7.9 kbp)

evidence.snippet: Our MT measurements used a 20.6 kbp DNA construct, based on the λ-phage DNA sequence, with a GC content of 46% and prepared as described previously [42, 43], unless stated otherwise.
Control measurements used a 7.9 kbp DNA construct with 56% GC content that was employed previously for similar measurements [6, 44].
PCR-generated DNA fragments (~600 bp) labeled with multiple biotin or digoxigenin groups were ligated to the DNA (20.6 kbp or 7.9 kbp)

A 0.1–5 M concentration of NaCl (99.5%, p.a., ACS, ISO; Carl Roth), 0.1–4 M KCl (99.5%, p.a., ACS, ISO; Carl Roth), 0.1–12 M LiCl (99%, p.a., ACS; Carl Roth), and 0.1–7 M CsCl (99.999%, p.a., Ultra Quality; Carl Roth) were prepared using 10 mM Tris (pH 7.0)

applies_to.transition: change in helical twist vs 100 mM KCl (LiCl, largest increase)

source.snippet: LiCl causes the largest twist increase, by ≤ 0.9° bp-1, compared with physiological salt, still far below the suggested C-form values of 2-3° bp-1.
